issues.description: Constructor parameter type mismatch for RollerCoaster: The UML in the problem statement (abstract class RollerCoaster) declares the attribute numberOfLoopings as int and thus the constructor is expected to accept an int for numberOfLoopings. The solution implementation declares the RollerCoaster constructor as public RollerCoaster(String name, char abbreviation, double numberOfLoopings) and casts it to int internally. This diverges from the UML/specification and is inconsistent with the subclass constructor in the solution (LaunchedRollerCoaster) which declares an int parameter and calls super(...). This inconsistency can confuse students about the expected constructor signature and types and about what they should implement to match the UML.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the RollerCoaster constructor parameter type to int to match the UML (e.g. public RollerCoaster(String name, char abbreviation, int numberOfLoopings)) and assign it directly to the int field without casting. Ensure any subclasses (e.g. LaunchedRollerCoaster) call super(...) with an int and that all repository artifacts (template and solution) use the same int signature so students implement the constructor exactly as specified in the UML.
